2 Heard Ms.Pooja who appears physically before this Court and represents Sri.Ravishankar Shastry.G,
learned counsel on record for the appellant.
Also heard Sri.L.Sreekanta Rao, learned counsel for respondent No.2 who appears through video conference.

2. Challenge in this appeal is the award that is passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-I,
Dakshina Kannada, Mangaluru in MVC No.230/2021 dated 03.08.2022.

entities.text:
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-I,
Dakshina Kannada, Mangaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: This is a claimant's appeal.
The appellant was awarded compensation of Rs.4,78,300/- through the impugned order.
His version is that he is entitled to a higher sum.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred in the year 2020.
As vegetable vendor he was earning around Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to the injury sustained, he lost his earnings.
But NC: 2026:KHC:6484 HC-KAR Tribunal failed to award the amount claimed and therefore, this appeal is filed.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.2 states that the award of the Tribunal is valid on all aspects.
Learned counsel submits that the Tribunal has taken into consideration each and every aspect of the case.
Learned counsel also states that in case this Court intends to enhance the sum that is awarded as compensation by the tribunal, there may be marginal enhancement.
5. By all the material that is brought on record, appellant succeeded in establishing that he sustained fracture of right femur and underwent a surgery.
He also established that he took treatment as inpatient for a period of 16 days.
Making an observation that the appellant might have lost earnings for 1 month, the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.14,500/- towards loss of earnings during laid up period.

However having considered NC: 2026:KHC:6484 HC-KAR the nature of injury sustained,
this Court is of the view that the appellant could not have attended his normal pursuits at least for a period of 3 months.

Furthermore, the compensation granted towards loss of amenities i.e.,
Rs.10,000/- is on lower side.
Also, the Tribunal has not granted any compensation for the expenses which the appellant would have incurred for his diet and attendant charges.
Therefore, taking into consideration all these aspects, this Court is of the view that appellant is entitled to an additional sum of Rs.50,000/- globally.

Hence the appeal is disposed of with the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) The compensation that is granted by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-I,
Dakshina Kannada, Mangaluru through orders in MVC No.230/2021 dated 03.08.2022 is enhanced by Rs.50,000/-.
